text: If you want to see the entire workflow as implemented by the New York Times there is a great documentary about it. [VIDEO] The documentary covers the last day that the NYT used a metal/linotype press and talks through the entire process that happened from newsroom to printing. It is a truly interesting way to spend 28 minutes.
Somewhat related - there's a good documentary about the last edition of the New York Times published using the linotype process called "Farewell Etaoin Shrdlu" [1]. [1] [VIDEO]

story: Why do we call it “boilerplate code?”
text: As an aside, check out the 30 minute documentary "Farewell Etaoin Shrdlu" ( [VIDEO] ) about the end of the linotype era. I'm amazed at the engineering that went into linotype printing.

story: Remembering a Programming Language That Helped Shape the Digital New York Times
text: When I was a ten year old kid in 1973 my school did a tour. I remember looking at some programs running on green-screen terminals, and the guy doing the demo typed in commands using the keyword FOR so I assume it was all Fortran back then.
